content.title: About
content.content: Cauliflower is an edible cruciferous vegetable obtained after boiling, steaming or roasting. Cooked cauliflower has a tender texture, a mild flavor, and retains most of its nutrients, including vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, and dietary fiber.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The white color of cauliflower florets gives it its name, though purple, orange and green varieties also exist.
In Japan it is often processed into "rice"‑like granules as a low‑carb alternative.
Cauliflower is rich in glucosinolates, which convert during cooking into compounds with anti‑cancer properties.
In ancient Roman cuisine it was sometimes referred to as "Brussels cabbage," a term now used for a different vegetable.

items.title: Rich source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cooked cauliflower is low‑calorie, making it a good choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Glucosinolates and carotenoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience an allergic reaction to cauliflower.

items.title: Thyroid concerns
items.content: Large amounts of raw cauliflower can affect thyroid function due to goitrogens; cooking reduces this effect.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Some individuals may experience increased gas or abdominal discomfort after eating cauliflower.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked cauliflower can be served as a side dish, added to soups, stews, salads, mashed, or used as a "rice" substitute. It pairs well with olive oil, garlic, lemon, and a variety of herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked cauliflower in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags after cooling.
